name: Shammah
title: David's Mighty Warrior
summary: Shammah, son of Agee the Hararite, was one of David's three mighty men. He is best known for his heroic stand when he alone defended a field of lentils against the Philistines while the rest of the people fled. His bravery was counted among the greatest feats in David's circle of elite warriors.

keyEvents.title: One of David's Three Mighty Men
keyEvents.description: Shammah is regarded as one of David's three mighty men, along with Jashobeam and Eleazar. These three distinguished themselves through extraordinary bravery.

keyEvents.title: The Defense of the Lentil Field
keyEvents.description: When the Philistines gathered at a plot of land full of lentils and the people fled, Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. The Lord brought about a great victory that day.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among David's Heroes in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Shammah is also mentioned in the parallel account in 1 Chronicles as part of David's foremost warriors and their deeds.

keyEvents.title: The Three Mighty Men Fetch Water from the Well of Bethlehem
keyEvents.description: In connection with the three heroes, it is told how they broke through the Philistine camp to fetch water from the well at Bethlehem's gate, which David longed for. David refused to drink the water and poured it out for the Lord.

keyEvents.title: A Model of Faithful Service
keyEvents.description: Shama's steadfastness when everyone else fled shows his deep loyalty to David and his calling as a warrior. His example was preserved as a testimony of courage and faithfulness.
